stories.headline: Tsahkna pushes EU-wide entry ban for Russian war veterans
stories.summary: Estonian Foreign Minister Margus Tsahkna advocated at EU foreign ministers meeting for bloc-wide entry bans on Russian soldiers who fought in Ukraine, arguing nearly one million combatants pose security risks to Europe. He coined the phrase 'There can be no path from Bucha to Brussels.'

stories.headline: Estonia considers eastern border closure after Russian illegal crossing
stories.summary: Foreign Minister Tsahkna said Estonia is weighing possible full closure of its eastern border with Russia as one response option to Russia's illegal border crossing last month, though no direct security threat has been identified yet.

articles.title: Estonia weighs possible eastern border closure after Russia crossing

stories.summary: Foreign Minister Tsahkna criticized former German chancellor Gerhard Schröder's attempts to change Europe's course back to old mistakes with Russia, rejecting calls to avoid 'demonizing' Russia and hints at renewed energy cooperation.

stories.headline: Parliament re-passes flexible working time legislation after presidential review
stories.summary: The Riigikogu re-adopted employment law amendments allowing flexible working time that President Alar Karis had declined to proclaim in early December, forcing parliament to reconsider the legislation.

stories.headline: Bank of Estonia gold reserves discussion amid global central bank buying
stories.summary: Analysis shows Estonia has sold most of its gold reserves while other central banks globally increase their holdings. Bank of Estonia holds only 256.6 kilograms compared to neighboring Finland's significant reserves worth 6.1 billion euros.

stories.summary: Testing of the new Kiisa battery park caused temporary disruption to Estonia-Finland electricity cables (Estlink). Grid operator Elering confirmed no security threat to supply but will review procedures for new market participants.
